newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion pulled down by world trends.
newsitem.headline: India bullion pulled down by world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 50 rupees lower at 4,480 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,530 rupees as losses in world markets prompted fresh selling. Gold was down by 20 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 600 rupees lower at 52,400 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Monday. They were down by 650 rupees per piece last week.

** Silver (.999) closed 50 rupees lower at 6,650 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,700 rupees amid sluggish industrial buying while a weak trend in world markets dragged local prices lower.
Gold 24 carat closed 50 rupees lower at 4,480 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,530 rupees as a weak trend in the world market triggered fresh selling, dealers said on Tuesday.
Gold was down by 20 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday.
"Sluggish physical demand also aided the weak sentiments but arrivals remained low today during the day," a dealer said.
"Looking at the eased supplies gold prices may bounce back from the current level," one broker said.
Meanwhile prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 600 rupees lower at 52,400 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees per piece on Monday. They were down 650 rupees last week.

Silver (.999) closed 50 rupees lower at 6,650 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,700 rupees amid fresh arrivals while weak trend in the world market as well as sluggish industrial demand prompted renewed offerings. Silver was steady on Monday after losing 60 rupees per kg during last week.
